en.title: Count Operations
en.description:
You are given a 1-based permutation p. One operation sets item i of the new array to item p[i] of the old array. For any array of distinct elements, find the number of repeated operations needed to restore the original array for the first time (at least one operation), modulo 1,000,000,007.

See the statement and review notes for the problem source and the input protocol added by this site.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains n integers p[i]. Source constraints: 1≤n≤100000, and p is a permutation of 1..n.
en.output: Output the minimum number of operations modulo 1,000,000,007.
en.explanation: Process the input according to the problem rules; see the accompanying notes for the detailed approach.
hints: Decompose the permutation into disjoint cycles. A cycle of length L returns to its original state only after a multiple of L operations, so the overall period is the least common multiple of all cycle lengths.
